title: Yapay Zekâ Destekli Anında Geri Bildirimin Lise Öğrencilerinin Başarı Motivasyonuna Etkisi
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether AI-supported instant feedback affects the academic achievement motivation of high school students. The study is motivated by the idea that timely, personalized feedback may support students’ motivation more effectively than traditional delayed teacher feedback, especially during adolescence. The authors frame the work using Self-Determination Theory, arguing that AI feedback may support autonomy, competence, and relatedness.

The intervention consisted of weekly composition-writing tasks completed over four weeks. Ninth-grade students in the experimental group used ChatGPT (GPT-4) on a school computer lab platform to receive immediate feedback on their writing, including grammar, language use, coherence, structure, and content suggestions. Students could review the feedback and revise their texts. The control group completed the same writing tasks but received delayed written feedback from their teacher once a week in the following lesson. The study reports that all students used the same model version and standardized prompting format, and that the teacher/researcher did not modify the AI-generated feedback.

The participants were 64 ninth-grade students in Istanbul, Türkiye, drawn from an accessible school and then randomly assigned to experimental (n=31) and control (n=33) groups. The study took place in the context of Turkish-language composition assignments, with topics including future aspirations, solution proposals, film/book review, and the importance of a value. Outcomes were measured with the Achievement Motivation Scale developed by Sarıtepeci (2018), administered as pretest and posttest.

The main conclusion is that AI-supported instant feedback substantially increased students’ self-reported academic achievement motivation compared with delayed teacher feedback. The groups did not differ significantly at pretest, but the posttest favored the experimental group with a very large reported effect. Cluster analysis further suggested that prior experience using AI tools may have shaped how strongly students benefited. However, the paper focuses on motivation rather than direct writing-quality outcomes, so it does not provide direct evidence about whether ChatGPT feedback improved essay quality, revision quality, or specific writing traits.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed pretest-posttest control-group experiment with random assignment to conditions, which is stronger than correlational evidence. However, it uses convenience sampling from one school, reports implausibly large posttest differences/effect size indications, and does not provide enough transparency on some statistical details, so it falls short of blue-tier credibility.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effect on achievement motivation is extremely large and clearly exceeds the threshold for a large impact, even though the magnitude should be interpreted cautiously because of reporting anomalies. The study also directly concerns a priority K-12 population (grade 9 secondary students) and compares AI feedback against teacher feedback.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT (GPT-4) provided immediate automated feedback on ninth-grade students' weekly composition drafts, including grammar, style, coherence, and content suggestions, with opportunities for iterative revision.
Students used ChatGPT as an AI-based conversational platform to receive real-time draft feedback during four weekly composition-writing tasks in Turkish class.

finding.finding_summary: In a pretest-posttest control-group experiment with ninth-grade students in Istanbul (n=64; experimental n=31, control n=33), students receiving ChatGPT-based instant feedback showed significantly higher posttest achievement motivation than peers receiving delayed teacher-written feedback. The paper reports posttest means of about 4.4 (SD=0.2) for the AI-feedback group versus 1.4 (SD=0.1) for the control group on the Achievement Motivation Scale, with a very large between-group effect (reported as Cohen's d very large; calculable from reported descriptives at roughly d≈19.0, suggesting reporting or scaling concerns).
finding.measure: Achievement Motivation Scale (Sarıtepeci, 2018), pretest and posttest Likert-scale motivation scores
finding.effect_size: reported as Cohen's d very large; estimable from reported posttest descriptives as d≈19.0
finding.std_deviation: experimental posttest SD=0.2; control posttest SD=0.1

finding.finding_summary: The intervention was implemented through four weekly composition-writing tasks ('My Dream Future,' 'Proposing a Solution to a Problem,' 'A Film/Book Review,' and 'The Importance of a Value'), and ChatGPT feedback targeted grammar, style, coherence, and content while allowing revision. However, the study did not report direct writing-quality outcome measures, scoring rubrics, interrater reliability, or comparative statistics for draft quality, so there is no direct secondary-school evidence here on whether ChatGPT feedback improved writing performance itself.
finding.measure: writing tasks/draft revision opportunities only; no direct scored writing outcome reported
